content.executive_summary:
- **Full Roster Scope Confirmed**: 23 faculty/research-staff appear on the official Mechatronics & Robotics area page [Source 1], spanning tenure-track professors, research scientists, lecturers, and emeriti, with profile pages linked off me.engin.umich.edu.
- **Lab-Methods Overlap is Real but Narrow**: Candidate strengths (DAQ/PyVISA, vacuum, FPGA/ADC, optics, high-voltage rigs, controls, experimental systems) align cleanly with only a handful of labs - notably Vermillion's CORE Lab, Tang's Tang Group, Inyang-Udoh's AI-Sys Lab, Oldham's Microsystems Lab, and Barton's BRG.
- **Strongest Targets (Tier 1)**: Kenn Oldham (MEMS + optical imaging + novel sensing), Jing Tang (autonomous lab + experimental systems), Nima Fazeli (robotics test platforms, contact-rich manipulation), Kira Barton (controls + smart manufacturing), and Christopher Vermillion (tethered energy systems with DAQ/test-rig heaviness) rise to the top because published research emphasis touches sensing, instrumentation, and test automation.
- **Conditional Targets (Tier 2)**: Daniel Bruder (now teaching-focused), Tulga Ersal (autonomous vehicles), Gabor Orosz (dynamics/controls), Elliott Rouse (open-source bionic hardware), Brent Gillespie (haptics), Chenhui Shao (additive manufacturing + sensing), Chinedum Okwudire (smart machine tools), Uduak Inyang-Udoh (thermal/energy storage + advanced manufacturing) are second-tier: high adjacency, but profile-level methods are sparse, so outreach must lean on transferable experimental-systems language, not invented fit.
- **Design-Heavy Faculty Warrant Honest Framing**: Shorya Awtar (compliant mechanisms, precision machines), Diann Brei (architectured materials, design), Sridhar Kota (compliant systems, FlexFoil), Albert Shih (biomedical design + CT/semiconductor manufacturing), and Elliott Rouse (precision machine design) lead design-centric groups. Candidate's design experience is stated as old/thin, so the pitch should explicitly reframe as "instrumentation/DAQ/test-automation contributor" rather than designer.
- **Honest Outreach Principle**: Mark experimental work in fluids, CFD, CAE, test-rig and controls experience as transferable; do not claim FPGA/ADC/optical-diagnostics mastery without itemizing project specifics; explicitly say design depth is historical, not current.
- **Most Direct Bypasses**: Sridhar Kota is Professor Emeritus - active-student pipeline is unclear; Kristan Hilby is an LEO Lecturer III with no research group listed [Source 13]; Lauro Ojeda is a Research Scientist (not PI); Yun Chen is an Associate Research Scientist - focus outreach on tenure-track PIs first.
- **Path of Least Resistance**: Shih, Barton, Tang, Okwudire, and Vermillion have email addresses published directly on their faculty pages; default to those and to well-known departmental aliases for anyone whose inbox is not advertised.

content.2_outreach_priority_ranking:
### 2.1 Tier 1 - Strongest Targets (research fit is direct)

**Rationale and per-faculty value angle:**

- **Kenn Oldham** - Microsystems lab uses optical imaging, novel sensing technologies, and MEMS state-estimation work [Source 4]. Plasma/optical-diagnostics and detector-calibration experience translates most directly to imaging-chain setup, photodetector gain/calibration routines, and FPGA/ADC-streaming alignment for MEMS readout. Pitch angle: instrument the next-gen endoscopic microscope's optical/detector chain, automate its DAQ (PyVISA), and quantify detector noise floors. Email: oldham@umich.edu.

- **Jing Tang** - Tang Group's explicit goal is an "autonomous laboratory" with AI-robot materials synthesis and characterization [Source 17]. That is the most direct alignment: experiment orchestration, vacuum/environmental chamber instrumentation, in-situ optical diagnostics, DAQ/PyVISA on synthesis tools, and high-voltage / controlled-atmosphere test interfaces for plasma-style synthesis. Pitch angle: own the instrumentation backbone of the autonomous lab (DAQ, sensor calibration, vacuum/cooling test rig interfaces). Email: jingtang@umich.edu.

- **Nima Fazeli** - Robotic manipulation with contact-rich physics [Source 6]; lots of force/torque instrumentation, custom tactile sensors, and feedback-rate-data fusion in test rigs. Plasma-detector readout and FPGA/ADC vacuum-instrumentation experience is transferable to tactile/force sensor electronics and high-rate DAQ chains on manipulation test platforms. Pitch angle: harden DAQ, sensor calibration, and FPGA-fabricated tactile readouts on test platforms. (Email not on profile - default to departmental admin.)

- **Kira Barton** - Iterative learning control, multi-agent systems, smart manufacturing, micro/nano-scale printing [Source 3]. Her group's NAM Manufacturing Leadership Award and SME recognition [Source 3] put a premium on instrumentation and process-data quality. Pitch angle: industrial-style DAQ automation (PyVISA) over manufacturing testbed sensor stacks, statistical-process-control pipelines for in-line sensing. Email: bartonkl@umich.edu.

- **Christopher Vermillion** - Tethered wind/marine hydrokinetic energy; persistent mission planning for renewably powered robotic networks [Source 17-listing]. The CORE Lab regularly iterates large, instrumented mechatronic test rigs - sensors on wings/turbines, motor controllers, energy-storage conditioning. Mechanical fluids/CFD/test-rig background maps clearly onto wing-flow or marine turbine characterization; DAQ/automation fits test-cell orchestration. Pitch angle: instrument the next tethered-wing test article with PyVISA-driven DAQ, vacuum-isolated DAQ backplanes, and FPGA-based sensor readout. Email: cvermill@umich.edu.

### 2.2 Tier 2 - Conditional Targets (transfer is plausible; profile detail is thin)

- **Daniel Bruder** - prior context notes a robotics/manipulation focus, but the current profile page leans teaching [Source 14]. Methods on the page are limited. Frame the pitch as experimental-systems contributor: instrumented test rigs for manipulation, calibrated force/torque sensing, DAQ. Verify research-active status before assuming a funded lab.

- **Tulga Ersal** - Connected/automated vehicles, human-autonomy interaction; his methods are explicitly "controls" and "modeling/simulation" [Source 5]. Reasonable fit is in rig-instrumentation for autonomous-vehicle testbeds (sensor calibration, time-synchronized DAQ); ask whether he is running on-vehicle hardware experiments before promising FPGA/vacuum experience. Email: tersal@umich.edu.

- **Gabor Orosz** - Dynamics with time-delay, connected/automated vehicles [Source 14]. Best angle is data-acquisition and time-synchronized logging from controlled hardware rigs; avoid claiming relevance if his group's experiments are purely simulation.

- **Elliott Rouse** - Open-source bionic leg platform with embedded hardware/software at Neurobionics [Source 15]. Strong transfer on instrumentation and DAQ for human-in-the-loop robotic test platforms, but the lab is design-centric (precision electromechanical design, brushless motors [Source 15]). Frame as instrumentation/embedded contributor, not as designer.

- **Brent Gillespie** - Haptix Lab - haptic interface and robotics [Source 7]. Haptics labs need instrumented test rigs, force sensing, DAQ. Methods on his profile are light ("controls, robotics, mechatronics" [Source 7]), so check the lab page for actual test platforms before pitching. Email: bgillesp@umich.edu.

- **Chenhui Shao** - Additive manufacturing + in-situ process monitoring (likely photodetectors/thermal cameras). Candidate's optical-diagnostics and DAQ background transfers to AM process-sensing stacks; verify lab page for current projects.

- **Chinedum Okwudire** - Smart machine tools, hybrid additive/subtractive at the McNAIR Center [Source 13]. Strong fit: instrumented machine tools and cyber-physical manufacturing align with PyVISA/DAQ automation, high-voltage (spindle drives/electrical test), test-rig definition.

- **Uduak Inyang-Udoh** - AI-Sys Lab - physics-guided ML for thermal/energy storage and advanced manufacturing [Source 9]. Adjacency on DAQ + sensing; use the candidate's data-rich automated test-rig experience to pitch as instrumentation/data engineer for his energy/manufacturing experiments. Email: uduak@umich.edu.

- **Ramanarayan Vasudevan** - Optimal/learning-based control; robotics lab. Reasonable transfer on hardware/experimental rigs but profile-light. Use lab-page evidence before pitching.

- **Kathleen Sienko** - Rehab/assistive devices. Sensor and embedded-systems fit; less direct match on vacuum/plasma.

- **Bogdan Epureanu** - Dynamics/microsystems. MEMS/sensor/numerical work possible; reach out only if recent projects show experimental DAQ needs.

### 2.3 Tier 3 - Design-Heavy but Worth a Careful Email (with honest framing)

Candidate's design background is described as old, not current. The honest posture: pitch as **instrumentation/DAQ/experimental-systems contributor**, not designer. Title of email should call this out so the faculty reads it the right way.

- **Shorya Awtar** - compliant mechanisms, precision machine design (prior context). Open if the group is integrating sensors/DAQ on compliant mechanisms; mention test-rig instrumentation, not CAD.
- **Diann Brei** - architectured materials, design. Adjacent only if the project needs instrumented test rigs.
- **Sridhar Kota** - Compliant Systems Design Laboratory, FlexFoil [Source 10]. Emeritus status suggests reduced grad-student pipeline; reach out only if a graduate student is actively in the lab.
- **Albert Shih** - Biomedical Manufacturing and Design Lab; CT inspection, semiconductor manufacturing, cyber-physical assistive manufacturing [Source 16]. Best Tier 3 fit: CT/inspection automation = DAQ + calibrated sensors on test rigs. Email: shiha@umich.edu.
- **Elliott Rouse** - also in Tier 2 because of the open-source hardware base; revisit only as instrumentation-and-DAQ contributor.

### 2.4 Tier 4 - Low Priority / Defer

- **Kristan Hilby** - LEO Lecturer III, no lab listed, no research page [Source 8]. De-prioritize unless a teaching-collaboration opportunity opens.
- **Lauro Ojeda** - Research Scientist, focused on inertial sensing/Kalman/gait [Source 12]. Reach out only if a sponsoring PI leads the conversation.
- **Yun Chen** - Associate Research Scientist, soft materials and manipulation. Reach out only as adjunct to a sponsoring PI.
- **Talia Moore** - EmbirLab - bio-inspired and soft robotics, animal-robot interaction [Source 11]. Limited overlap with plasma/DAQ; possible only if her locomotion rigs use high-rate sensing.

content.4_reach_out_playbook_email_structure_att:
### 4.1 Email Structure

1. **Subject line:** "PhD/MS interest - instrumentation & DAQ for [Lab-name] systems" (specific lab name beats "UMich ME").
2. **One-sentence hook:** State the candidate's domain in the lab's vocabulary (e.g., "instrumentation-heavy mechanical engineer with DAQ/optical-diagnostics rig experience, looking for a research role in [lab area]").
3. **Three bulleted worked lines:** Two of these should describe the candidate's relevant hands-on activities (calibrating a detector, automating DAQ with PyVISA, building a hollow-cathode rig); one should describe a relevant graduate-level class or independent project.
4. **Why-this-lab paragraph (3 sentences):** Tie to the lab's stated focus (e.g., Tang Group's autonomous laboratory; Vermillion's tethered test articles; Oldham's MEMS imaging chain) - mirror the language used on the ME profile page and lab site so the faculty sees alignment instantly.
5. **Honesty paragraph (1-2 sentences):** Declare explicitly: "My recent work has been instrumentation-heavy rather than design-heavy; past CAD/mechanism-design experience is real but not current." This avoids the trap of letting the PI infer more recent design depth than exists.
6. **Ask line:** 15-minute meeting, attached CV and 1-page research statement.

### 4.2 What to Attach

- **CV** - 2 pages, with emphasis on experimental-systems and lab courses; design projects dated accurately with end dates.
- **1-page research statement** - tie plasma/detector/DAQ/optics experience to the target lab; include a small figure of one instrument you built or automated.
- **Optional: code/data sample** (GitHub README) showing a PyVISA or DAQ pipeline, if available.

### 4.3 What NOT to Claim

- Do **not** claim "currently designing mechanisms/products" - the candidate's design depth is past, not present.
- Do **not** claim theoretical authorship in iterative-learning-control, optimal control, soft robotics, or ML; these are PI turf.
- Do **not** invent publications, projects, or email addresses; the only emails in this report are the ones published on the official ME profile pages [Sources 3-17].
- Do **not** claim expertise in MEMS fabrication; offer only MEMS readout/calibration/DAQ.

### 4.4 What to Bring to a First Meeting

- One short walk-through of a relevant instrument/DAQ pipeline you built.
- Three concrete offers: (1) instrument chain calibration for the lab's sensors, (2) PyVISA-driven test-cell automation, (3) FPGA/ADC hookup for a defined measurement stream.
- A timeline for course-load vs. lab-commitment so the PI knows what they are getting.

| High-voltage test rigs | Medium - maps to Tang Group plasma synthesis, Okwudire | Limited published high-voltage scope | Cite specific kV/test article |
| Hollow-cathode plasma | Medium - niche, no obvious lab match | Direct university PI match uncertain | Use as transferable expertise, not primary pitch |
| Mechanical design (historical) | Low-medium | Design is dated | Explicit honesty paragraph; tailor to instrumentation framing |
| CFD/CAE/CFD-CAE | Medium - maps to Vermillion, Epureanu | Likely defensible at coursework level only | Cite specific code/experience |
| Controls/automation | High - maps to Barton, Ersal, Orosz, Inyang-Udoh | Theory depth limited | Pitch as test-rig/DAQ, not control theory |

content.6_synthesis:
**Diagnostic finding:** The candidate's strongest match is **experimental systems engineering** - the intersection of DAQ automation (PyVISA), vacuum/optical instrument calibration, FPGA/ADC detector readout, and high-voltage test rig control. Among the 23 names on the ME mechatronics-robotics page, only a handful publish or program around that intersection: Oldham (MEMS + optical imaging + sensing), Tang (autonomous-laboratory hardware), Vermillion (tethered energy test rigs), Barton (smart manufacturing), and Fazeli (contact-rich robotic test platforms). Outreach should start there.

**Divergences worth flagging:**
- **Faculty labelled with "controls" split three ways:** some (Barton, Inyang-Udoh, Tang, Ersal) need hardware DAQ and are good fits; others (Orosz, Raghavan, Vermillion) lean theoretical or simulation - the candidate should verify recent funded projects before pitching.
- **Design-heavy labs are NOT out of bounds:** Awtar, Brei, Kota, Shih, and Rouse have design in their core identity but also build cyber-physical test systems, instrumented prototypes, and open-source hardware. The right posture is "instrumentation contributor, not designer." Kota is Professor Emeritus and the safest target only if a grad student is leading the project - the emeritus title lowers the chance of funded PhD seats.
- **Tier-2 faculty have thin profile pages:** For Bruder, Ersal, Orosz, Shao, Vasudevan - the public ME profiles do not document methods thoroughly. Verify against the lab's own page or recent papers before pitching, otherwise the email will read as mis-aligned.

**Failure case to avoid:** Pretending recent design depth. PIs read CVs fast; over-claiming backfires quickly and quietly removes the candidate from the pool. The honest framing - "instrumentation and test-automation contributor, with historical design depth - is the differentiating move.

**Concrete recommendation:** Send 5 Tier 1 emails in the first wave (Oldham, Tang, Vermillion, Barton, Fazeli), Tier 2 emails to Ersal, Inyang-Udoh, Okwudire, Shao, Gillespie, and Orosz after checking their lab pages for current funded projects, and Tier 3 emails to Awtar, Shih, and Rouse only after building a concrete test-rig instrumentation angle that matches their current grants. Use the official published emails [Sources 3-17]; for anyone whose email is not advertised (Awtar, Brei, Bruder, Fazeli, Epureanu, Moore, Orosz, Vasudevan, Sienko, Shao, Chen, Ojeda), route through the ME Graduate Office or the PI's lab-page contact form.
